facts.statement: The genus Prognathodon was first described by Louis Dollo in 1889.
facts.quote: authority: Dollo, 1889

facts.statement: Fossils of Prognathodon date from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian stages.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Campanian - Maastrichtian,

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Prognathodon solvayi.
facts.quote: type_species: Prognathodon solvayi

facts.statement: Several names have been used as synonyms for Prognathodon, including Prognathosaurus, Dollosaurus, Brachysaurana, and Tenerasaurus.
facts.quote: synonyms: * Prognathosaurus (Dollo, 1889) (Williston, 1897) Dollosaurus (Yakovlev, 1905) Brachysaurana (Strand, 1926) Ancylocentrum (Schmidt, 1927) Tenerasaurus (Kaddumi, 2009) Tylosaurus capensis (Broom, 1912) Taniwhasaurus capensis (Broom, 1912)

facts.statement: Prognathodon is classified within the Mosasaurinae subfamily, near genera such as Mosasaurus and Clidastes.
facts.quote: It is classified as part of the Mosasaurinae subfamily, alongside genera like Mosasaurus and Clidastes.

facts.statement: Remains of Prognathodon have been found in the Middle East, Europe, New Zealand, Africa, and North America.
facts.quote: Prognathodon has been recovered from deposits ranging in age from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian in the Middle East, Europe, New Zealand, Africa and North America.

facts.statement: The name Prognathodon translates to "forejaw tooth" from Latin and Greek roots.
facts.quote: Prognathodon means "forejaw tooth", which originates from the Latin pro- ("earlier" or "prior"), Greek gnathos ("jaw") and odṓn ("tooth").

facts.statement: Prognathodon is characterized by its massively built jaws and teeth.
facts.quote: Prognathodon is known for its massively built jaws and teeth.

facts.statement: The initial description of Prognathodon was based on specimens collected in Belgium.
facts.quote: Prognathodon was first described by Louis Dollo in 1889 based on specimens gathered in Belgium.

facts.statement: An intact fossil skull of Prognathodon was discovered in Maastricht limestone quarries in 1998.
facts.quote: In 1998, an intact fossil skull was found in the Maastricht limestone quarries.

facts.statement: A 12-meter-long Prognathodon skeleton nicknamed "Bèr" is displayed at the Natural History Museum in Maastricht.
facts.quote: This specimen was the first reasonably complete mosasaur specimen recovered from the Maastricht area since 1957; the skeleton is on display at the Natural History Museum at Maastricht, and is from an animal that was probably 12 metres long.

facts.statement: A large specimen from Israel was originally informally called "Oronosaurus" before being classified as Prognathodon currii.
facts.quote: A very large specimen found in Israel was for some time informally named "Oronosaurus", but eventually described as a new species of Prognathodon, P. currii.

facts.statement: The first fully articulated skeletons of Prognathodon were described in 2011 from Alberta, Canada.
facts.quote: Two specimens of Prognathodon overtoni described in 2011 from the early late Campanian (c. 74.5 Ma) Bearpaw Formation in Alberta, Canada provided the first fully articulated skeletons of the genus.

facts.statement: Prognathodon hudae was described in 2009 from fossils found in Harrana, Jordan.
facts.quote: In 2009, Hani F. Kaddumi described the new species P. hudae based on a complete right dentary and partial left dentary from the Maastrichtian-age Muwaqqar Chalk Marl Formation of Harrana, Jordan.

facts.statement: A 1.8-meter-long juvenile Prognathodon fossil preserves the outline of a bilobed tail fluke, resembling a shark's tail.
facts.quote: This fossil is about 1.8 m in length, and is remarkable in that it preserves the outline of the mosasaur's tail fins, revealing that Prognathodon had a bilobed tail fluke resembling a downturned shark's tail.

facts.statement: A Prognathodon skeleton nicknamed "Carlo" was discovered in September 2012 in the same quarry where the type specimen of Mosasaurus hoffmanni was found.
facts.quote: On 19 September 2012, it was announced that nine days earlier, again a skeleton of what appears to be a Mosasaur was found in the limestone quarry just outside Maastricht, the same quarry that yielded the type specimen of Mosasaurus hoffmanni.

facts.statement: The "Carlo" specimen is estimated to be 67.83 million years old, making it older than the "Bèr" specimen.
facts.quote: Based on stratigraphy, the age of the specimen was estimated at 67.83 million years, making it about one-and-a-half million years older than "Bèr".

facts.statement: The "Carlo" specimen appears to be the oldest known Mosasaurid from the Maastricht area.
facts.quote: From what has been uncovered, this appears to be the oldest known Mosasaurid specimen from the Maastricht area, and it belongs to the genus Prognathodon.

facts.statement: The classification of species within Prognathodon is controversial due to differences between specimens and incomplete fossil records.
facts.quote: Due to the sometimes clear differences between them and the incomplete nature of many of the specimens, the systematics of the genus and which species should properly be considered Prognathodon is controversial.

facts.statement: Direct evidence of Prognathodon's diet, such as gastric residues, is rare despite its distinct feeding adaptations.
facts.quote: Its distinct feeding adaptations have generated much interest in its ecology ever since its discovery, though direct evidence of its diet, such as gastric residues, is rare.

facts.statement: A 2022 study reclassified T. capensis as a chimera of Prognathodon and Taniwhasaurus, though it could not be identified to the species level.
facts.quote: An anatomical review of South African mosasaurs by Woolley et al. (2022) reclassified T. capensis, originally assigned to Tylosaurus and later to Taniwhasaurus, as a chimera of two different mosasaur genera (cf. Prognathodon and cf. Taniwhasaurus), but not identifiable at the species level.

facts.statement: Prognathodon is one of the largest mosasaur genera, with the largest known skull measuring over 1.4 meters in length.
facts.quote: Prognathodon constitutes one of the largest-bodied mosasaur genera, with the largest known skull (belonging to P. currii) exceeding 1.4 m in length.

facts.statement: The type species Prognathodon solvayi was the smallest in the genus, reaching approximately 5 to 6 meters in length.
facts.quote: The type species, P. solvayi, was the smallest, reaching around 5 - 6 m in length.

facts.statement: In 1967, Prognathodon giganteus was estimated to reach 10 meters in length.
facts.quote: In 1967, P. giganteus was estimated to have reached 10 m in length.

facts.statement: In 2002, Christiansen and Bonde estimated the maximum length of Prognathodon currii at 11 meters.
facts.quote: In 2002, Christiansen and Bonde estimated the maximum length of P. currii at 11 m.

facts.statement: Based on a 2002 study, Schupl and colleagues estimated that Prognathodon saturator could reach 12 meters in length.
facts.quote: Considering this 2002 study, Schupl and colleagues estimated that P. saturator would have reached 12 m in length.

facts.statement: Prognathodon hudae is estimated to have reached 6.4 meters in length.
facts.quote: P. hudae is estimated to have reached 6.4 m in length.

facts.statement: The largest known specimen of Prognathodon overtoni measures over 7 to 8 meters in length.
facts.quote: The largest P. overtoni specimen is TMP 2018.042.0005, a nearly completely preserved individual measuring over 7 - 8 m in length.

facts.statement: Prognathodon sectorius is estimated to have been about 8 meters in length.
facts.quote: P. sectorius would have approached the same size, about 8 m in length.

facts.statement: All species of Prognathodon possess scleral rings, a defining feature of the genus.
facts.quote: Other than its size and robust nature, another feature that defines Prognathodon is the form of the scleral rings, present in all species of the genus.

facts.statement: In Prognathodon solvayi, the preserved scleral ring consists of five scleral ossicles per ring.
facts.quote: In the type species, P. solvayi, the scleral ring is only partially preserved, consisting of five scleral ossicles in each ring.

facts.statement: The dentary of Prognathodon contains thirteen to fourteen teeth, while the pterygoid has seven to eight teeth.
facts.quote: The dentary itself contains thirteen to fourteen teeth and the pterygoid has seven to eight teeth.

facts.statement: The marginal teeth of Prognathodon are stout, bicarinate, and either smooth or striated.
facts.quote: The marginal teeth are stout, bicarinate and smooth or striated.

facts.statement: Prognathodon is characterized by a very robust skull.
facts.quote: Prognathodon is noted as having a very robust skull.

facts.statement: The skull of Prognathodon shows adaptations for very powerful jaw musculature.
facts.quote: The skull also shows adaptations towards a very powerful jaw musculature.

facts.statement: In 1998, Kase and colleagues estimated that Prognathodon overtoni had an anterior bite force of 6,346 to 9,127 Newtons and a posterior bite force of 7,630 to 10,974 Newtons.
facts.quote: In 1998, Kase and colleagues estimated that P. overtoni had an anterior bite force of 6346 - 9127 N and a posterior bite force of 7630 - 10974 N.

facts.statement: The ratio of supratemporal fenestra length to skull length is relatively high in Prognathodon (0.22 in P. overtoni and P. saturator) compared to Mosasaurus (0.19 in M. hoffmannii).
facts.quote: The ratio between the length of the supratemporal fenestra and the total length of the skull has previously been used as an improvised measurement for mosasaur bite force, and is relatively high in Prognathodon (0.22 in P. overtoni and P. saturator) compared to other genera, such as Mosasaurus (0.19 in M. hoffmannii).

facts.statement: The quadrates of Prognathodon have fused suprastapedial and infrastapedial processes, possibly an adaptation to withstand strong biting forces.
facts.quote: The quadrates of Prognathodon, similarly to the genus Globidens, have fused suprastapedial and infrastapedial processes, which is possibly an adaptation to counteract the strong forces experienced by the bone during biting.

facts.statement: Strong jaw musculature combined with a short and tall dentary likely resulted in a very powerful bite for Prognathodon.
facts.quote: Strong jaw musculature combined with a relatively short and tall dentary would have resulted in a very powerful bite.

facts.statement: The marginal teeth of Prognathodon are massive, smooth, and rounded, unlike the typically facetted and laterally compressed teeth of most other mosasaurs.
facts.quote: The marginal teeth are massive, smooth and rounded as opposed to most other mosasaur teeth, which are typically facetted and laterally compressed.

facts.statement: The dentaries of Prognathodon lutugini are fused with the splenial and prearticular, contain 13 teeth, and at least eight possess subdental crypts with replacement teeth found in the type specimen.
facts.quote: The dentaries are fused with the posterior end of the splenial and the anterior blade of the prearticular and have a tooth count of 13, with at least eight teeth possessing subdental crypts with some replacement teeth having been found in the type specimen.

facts.statement: The coronoid bone in Prognathodon lutugini is saddle-shaped with a well-developed posterodorsal process creating a nearly 110-degree angle.
facts.quote: The coronoid is saddle-shaped and has a well-developed posterodorsal process, which gives the dorsal margin of said bone a nearly 110 degree angle between the horizontal anterior end and the subvertical posterior wing.

facts.statement: Some researchers classify Prognathodon lutugini in its own genus, Dollosaurus, while others place it within Prognathodon.
facts.quote: This combination of characteristics aided in determining that P. lutugini was indeed a species of Prognathodon, since some researchers place it in a genus of its own, "Dollosaurus".

facts.statement: Typical Prognathodon teeth are robust, conical, and feature blunt serrated edges with smooth enamel.
facts.quote: Robust and conical teeth with blunt, serrated carinae and smooth enamel are often seen as typical Prognathodon teeth

facts.statement: The type species P. solvayi possesses 12 teeth in the upper jaw and 13 in the lower jaw.
facts.quote: P. solvayi has 12 teeth on the maxilla and 13 on the dentary

facts.statement: The species P. overtoni has 14 teeth in its lower jaw.
facts.quote: P. overtoni has 14 dentary teeth

facts.statement: The largest known tooth crowns of P. lutugini reach a height of 5.5 cm and a base width of 2.5 cm.
facts.quote: The largest known tooth crowns are up to 5.5 cm tall and 2.5 cm wide at the base

facts.statement: Anterior pterygoid teeth in P. lutugini can be as large as 4.6 cm in height, comparable to the marginal teeth.
facts.quote: Anterior pterygoid teeth are noted for being relatively large and comparable to the marginal teeth in size at up to 4.6 cm in height

facts.statement: The type specimen of P. lutugini preserves four cervical vertebrae with well-developed anterior and posterior zygapophyses.
facts.quote: Four cervical vertebrae are preserved, which have well-developed anterior and posterior zygapophyses

facts.statement: The preserved cervical vertebrae of P. lutugini measure approximately 7.2 cm in length and 4 cm in height.
facts.quote: The cervical vertebrae are almost the same size as the longest dorsal vertebrae and get to a length of about 7.2 cm and a height of 4 cm

facts.statement: The type specimen of P. lutugini includes 26 preserved dorsal vertebrae.
facts.quote: 26 dorsal vertebrae are preserved in the specimen

facts.statement: The dorsal vertebrae of P. lutugini reach a maximum length of 8 cm and a height of 5 cm.
facts.quote: The dorsal vertebrae are at a maximum about 8 cm in length and 5 cm in height

facts.statement: Evidence from Prognathodon fossils supports the theory that mosasaurs evolved a crescent-shaped tail fluke convergently with ichthyosaurs, thalattosuchians, and whales.
facts.quote: This helped in providing evidence that mosasaurs were convergent with ichthyosaurs, metriorhynchid thalattosuchians and whales in the evolution of a crescent-shaped tail fluke to aid in locomotion

facts.statement: The tail fluke of Prognathodon was asymmetric, with a lower lobe that followed the vertebrae and had a streamlined cross-section.
facts.quote: The tail fluke is clearly asymmetric. The lower fin lobe follows the caudal vertebrae and would have had a streamlined cross-section in life

facts.statement: The upper lobe of the Prognathodon tail fluke was unsupported by bone and appears as a small, wing-like structure above the vertebrae.
facts.quote: The upper fin lobe is unsupported by the skeleton and is preserved as a small, almost wing-like, structure above the last few caudal vertebrae

facts.statement: The Prognathodon tail fluke shape resembles that of carcharhinid sharks but is inverted, featuring a small upper lobe and a large lower lobe.
facts.quote: The shape of the tail fluke is similar to that of the carcharhinid sharks, though turned upside down, with a small upper lobe and large lower lobe

facts.statement: Scale impressions on the Prognathodon specimen reveal a rhomboidal shape.
facts.quote: These impressions reveal scales of "rhomboidal" shape

facts.statement: Research suggests the upper fin lobe of Prognathodon would have grown proportionally larger in bigger individuals.
facts.quote: Lindgren et al. (2013) especially noted that the upper fin lobe likely would have grown to be proportionally larger in bigger individuals

facts.statement: Modern phylogenetic analyses consistently classify Prognathodon within the Mosasaurinae subfamily.
facts.quote: Modern phylogenetic analyses continually place Prognathodon within the Mosasaurinae subfamily

facts.statement: Gorden L. Bell Jr. was the first to recover Prognathodon within the Mosasaurinae as a close relative of Globidens and Plesiotylosaurus.
facts.quote: Bell recovered Prognathodon within the Mosasaurinae, for the first time ever, as a close relative of the genera Globidens and Plesiotylosaurus

facts.statement: Gorden L. Bell Jr. was the first to note that Prognathodon is paraphyletic rather than monophyletic.
facts.quote: Bell was also the first to note that his analysis recovered Prognathodon, previously believed to be monophyletic, as paraphyletic

facts.statement: Recent analyses, including those by Cau and Madzia (2017) and Simões et al. (2017), recover Prognathodon as a sister group to the Mosasaurini.
facts.quote: Within Cau and Madzia's analysis (as well as previous work such as Simões et al., 2017), Prognathodon is recovered as a sister group to the Mosasaurini

facts.statement: Lindgren (2005) noted that the type species P. solvayi has labio-lingually compressed and gently facetted teeth, deviating from the typical robust, conical teeth assigned to the genus.
facts.quote: Lindgren (2005) pointed out that robust and conical tooth crowns with blunt, serrated carinae and smooth enamel are routinely assigned to the genus, despite the generic type species, P. solvayi deviating from that description since it exhibits markedly labio-lingually compressed and gently facetted marginal teeth

facts.statement: P. solvayi is the type species of Prognathodon and is the smallest known species, reaching barely 5 meters in length.
facts.quote: P. solvayi is the type species of Prognathodon and also the smallest known species at barely 5 meters in length

facts.statement: P. lutugini differs from all other Prognathodon species except P. solvayi by having 13 teeth in its dentary.
facts.quote: P. lutugini also differs from all other species except for P. solvayi by having 13 teeth in its dentary

facts.statement: Prognathodon giganteus was described by Dollo in 1904 from Maastrichtian deposits in Belgium, Jordan, and Syria.
facts.quote: Prognathodon giganteus Dollo, 1904 — Maastrichtian, Belgium, Jordan and Syria

facts.statement: P. lutugini was originally named as a species of Clidastes by Yakovlev in 1901 based on an incomplete skull and skeleton (specimen CNIGR 818).
facts.quote: P. lutugini was originally named as a species of Clidastes by Yakovlev in 1901 based on the type specimen CNIGR 818, an incomplete skull and skeleton

facts.statement: Yakovlev erected the genus Dollosaurus in 1905, named in honor of the Belgian paleontologist Louis Dollo.
facts.quote: Yakovlev erected a new genus in 1905, Dollosaurus, named in honor of the belgian paleontologist Louis Dollo

facts.statement: P. lutugini is unique among Prognathodon species (except P. solvayi) for having 13 teeth in its dentary.
facts.quote: P. lutugini also differs from all other species except for P. solvayi by having 13 teeth in its dentary

facts.statement: Excluding controversial species limits Prognathodon's range to Europe and the Middle East and removes any occurrence before the Late Campanian.
facts.quote: Notably, the exclusion of the six controversial species significantly shortens both the temporal and geographical range of the genus, limiting it to Europe and the Middle East and removing any occurrence before the Late Campanian

facts.statement: Lindgren (2005) noted that the placement of P. lutugini is unclear, with dental and osteological features suggesting Prognathodon but laterally pitted caudal vertebrae suggesting a more distant relation.
facts.quote: Lindgren (2005) noted that the taxonomic situation of P. lutugini (or "Dollosaurus") was somewhat unclear and that dental and osteological features suggested a placement within Prognathodon whilst the laterally pitted caudal vertebrae suggested a more distant relation

facts.statement: The controversy over whether Prognathodon is paraphyletic complicates the classification of material referred to P. lutugini.
facts.quote: Furthermore, the controversy surrounding whether the genus Prognathodon is paraphyletic or not complicated a better look at the classification of the material referred to P. lutugini

facts.statement: Recent phylogenetic analyses suggest that several species previously classified as Prognathodon actually belong to different genera.
facts.quote: the latest phylogenetic analyses, such as Madzia and Cau (2017) and Simões et al. (2017), recover said species as outside the genus Prognathodon

facts.statement: Prognathodon kianda is unique among its relatives for having a high number of marginal teeth and relatively small pterygoid teeth.
facts.quote: P. kianda is known from the Maastrichtian of Angola and is unique in possessing a high marginal tooth count and relatively small pterygoid teeth

facts.statement: Prognathodon overtoni is distinguished by the smooth enamel on its teeth and their non-procumbant nature.
facts.quote: P. overtoni can be distinguished from other species, including P. solvayi, by the smooth enamel of its teeth and their non-procumbant nature

facts.statement: Fossils of Prognathodon overtoni have preserved gut contents, offering insight into its diet.
facts.quote: some of which even preserve gut contents

facts.statement: Prognathodon rapax can be easily distinguished from other species by specific characters found in the quadrate bone.
facts.quote: P. rapax is easily separated from species P. overtoni and P. solvayi by characters in the quadrate

facts.statement: Prognathodon saturator was a massively built and enormous species that lived in the Maastrichtian of the Netherlands.
facts.quote: P. saturator is a massively built and enormous species from the Maastrichtian of the Netherlands

facts.statement: Prognathodon saturator reached lengths of approximately 9 to 10 meters.
facts.quote: P. saturator reached lengths of approximately 9-10 meters

facts.statement: The most obvious distinguishing feature of Prognathodon saturator is its massive size compared to other species of the genus.
facts.quote: The most obvious distinguishing feature of P. saturator that separates it from other species of Prognathodon is its massive size

facts.statement: Unlike other members of the genus, Prognathodon saturator lacks a high crest on the dorsal median ridge.
facts.quote: P. saturator also lacks the high crest on the dorsal median ridge which is found in other members of the genus

facts.statement: Prognathodon stadtmani, from the Early Campanian, is characterized by a much more slender dentary.
facts.quote: The Early Campanian P. stadtmani has a much more slender dentary

facts.statement: The robustness of the quadrate bone and mandible suggests that Prognathodon saturator could achieve bite forces greater than any other known mosasaur.
facts.quote: the robustness of the quadrate bone, along with the equally robust mandible, suggests that P. saturator could achieve bite forces in excess of all other mosasaurs

facts.statement: Healed bite marks suggest that Prognathodon saturator preyed on large sea turtles up to 2.9 meters long.
facts.quote: it is possible (based on found healed bite marks) that the size range of the prey of P. saturator included these 2.9 meter long turtles

facts.statement: In 2019, researchers suggested that Liodon mosasauroides might belong to the genus Eremiasaurus based on unpublished morphological comparisons.
facts.quote: In 2019 it was suggested by Mohr et al. that mosasauroides may perhaps be referable to the Maastrichtian-age genus Eremiasaurus based on unpublished morphological comparisons

facts.statement: Some researchers have suggested that certain species formerly assigned to Liodon are actually closer to Mosasaurus than to Prognathodon.
facts.quote: Palci et al. (2014) however suggested the possibility that these three species, and perhaps also the type species of Liodon (L. anceps) were closer to Mosasaurus than to Prognathodon

facts.statement: In 2020, Prognathodon stadtmani was redescribed as the type species of the new genus Gnathomortis.
facts.quote: The species P. stadtmani was redescribed as the type species of its own genus, Gnathomortis, in 2020

facts.statement: Evidence suggests that Prognathodon's internal body temperature was likely higher than the surrounding seawater.
facts.quote: Its internal body temperature was likely higher the surrounding seawater as well

facts.statement: Specimens of Prognathodon overtoni found in Alberta, Canada, contained gut contents including large fish, small fish, a sea turtle, and possibly a cephalopod.
facts.quote: The discovery of well-preserved specimens of Prognathodon overtoni in the Campanian Bearpaw Formation of Alberta, Canada allowed detailed studies of the gut contents (including fragments of a large and a small fish, a sea turtle and potentially a cephalopod) and dentition which allowed speculation into the ecology of Prognathodon.

facts.statement: Researchers hypothesize that Prognathodon was adapted to crush hard-shelled prey based on its roughened teeth and the presence of turtle bones in its gut.
facts.quote: The blunt tip and roughened surface suggest a tooth that was used for capturing fairly hard prey, and the presence of turtle bones as gut contents lends support to the hypothesis that Prognathodon was adapted to crush through hard-shelled prey.

facts.statement: Serrated ridges on Prognathodon's teeth suggest it was an opportunistic predator similar to modern killer whales rather than one specialized for crushing prey.
facts.quote: The presence of serrated carinae would suggest that Prognathodon instead was an opportunistic predator comparable to modern killer whales, rather than particularly adapted to crush its prey.

facts.statement: Prognathodon overtoni was likely an opportunistic apex predator capable of feeding on nearly anything in the Western Interior Seaway.
facts.quote: Prognathodon overtoni, likely similar in ecology to other species of the genus, was thus likely an opportunistic predator capable of feeding upon nearly anything in the Western Interior Seaway.

facts.statement: The specimen TMP 2007.034.0001 is the first Prognathodon fossil to preserve preserved gut contents.
facts.quote: One of the Alberta specimens, TMP 2007.034.0001, is the first Prognathodon specimen with preserved gut contents.

facts.statement: The sharply curved and short posteriormost teeth of Prognathodon were unlikely used for capturing or processing prey.
facts.quote: The posteriormost teeth are sharply curved and short and were thus unlikely to have been used for prey capture or food processing.

facts.statement: Large anterior pterygoid teeth in Prognathodon likely allowed it to grip and swallow large pieces of prey.
facts.quote: The large anterior pterygoid teeth that characterize Prognathodon likely provided an effective grip on large food items, indicating that the genus was capable of swallowing prey in large pieces.

facts.statement: The likely cause of death for the type specimen of Prognathodon saturator was age or disease, as no large marine predators are known from the Maastrichtian.
facts.quote: The likely cause of death of the specimen was age or disease, due to marine predators large enough to kill something of its size being unknown from the Maastrichtian.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Prognathodon saturator shows evidence of scavenging by sharks of the genera Squalicorax and Plicatoscyllium.
facts.quote: Evidence of shark scavenging include the finds of associated teeth of shark genera Squalicorax and Plicatoscyllium among the bones of the mosasaur.

facts.statement: A Prognathodon specimen nicknamed "Carlo," discovered in the Netherlands and described in 2020, had severe facial deformities including a partial amputation of the premaxilla.
facts.quote: A Prognathodon specimen known as NHMM 2012 (often nicknamed as "Carlo"), described by Bastiaans et al. in the journal Cretaceous Research in 2020, was discovered in the Netherlands near Maastricht, and was shown to have severe facial deformities including a devastating partial amputation of the premaxilla.

facts.statement: The specimen "Carlo" shows signs of bone regrowth and ongoing infection, suggesting the injuries were inflicted by another mosasaur.
facts.quote: This specimen shows signs of regrowth of bone around the injury as well as subsequent infections that were ongoing at the time of the mosasaur's death, which may have been partially caused by the injuries inflicted.

facts.statement: The mosasaur specimen "Carlo" showed a mammal-like immune response to infection, including liquid pus, unlike modern reptiles.
facts.quote: Unlike modern reptilians where solid fibrous masses are produced to contain infections, this mosasaur showed a much more mammal-like response, including liquid pus.

facts.statement: The genus Prognathodon was described by Dollo in 1889.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Dollo, 1889

facts.statement: Prognathodon lived during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Cretácico Superior

facts.statement: Prognathodon lived during the Late Cretaceous in what is now North America, Europe, and Africa.
facts.quote: Prognathodon es un género extinto de saurópsidos mosasáuridos que vivieron durante el Cretácico Superior, en lo que actualmente es Norteamérica, Europa, y África.

facts.statement: Prognathodon possessed bony rings around its eye orbits, indicating it lived in deep waters.
facts.quote: Poseía anillos óseos rodeando sus órbitas oculares, lo que indica que vivía en aguas profundas.

facts.statement: Prognathodon was characterized by a large, relatively short, and acinetic skull with a rounded snout tip.
facts.quote: Se caracterizaba por un cráneo grande y relativamente corto. El cráneo era acinético, con una punta del hocico redondeada.

facts.statement: Prognathodon had large conical teeth, with those located in the pterygoid being very large.
facts.quote: Los dientes son grandes, cónicos, y los ubicados en el pterigoides eran muy grandes.

facts.statement: In some species, Prognathodon's teeth extended forward like placodonts, suggesting a similar lifestyle of eating shellfish, large fish, and sea turtles, though it was generally a generalist predator.
facts.quote: En algunas especies los dientes se extendían hacia adelante, como algunos de los placodontes que vivieron durante el Triásico, por lo que pueden haber tenido un estilo de vida parecido, alimentándose de mariscos, peces grandes y tortugas marinas, aunque en general serían depredadores generalistas.

facts.statement: The name Prognathodon comes from Greek, meaning "tooth protruding from the jaw," referring to teeth that extended beyond the jaw.
facts.quote: Estos dientes que sobresalían de la mandíbula son la razón del nombre de Prognathodon (en griego, "diente sobresaliendo de la mandíbula").

facts.statement: Fossil remains of Prognathodon have been found in the United States, Canada, Belgium, New Zealand, Morocco, Angola, and the Netherlands.
facts.quote: Sus restos fósiles han sido hallados en los Estados Unidos (Dakota del Sur y Colorado), Canadá (Alberta), Bélgica, Nueva Zelanda, Marruecos, Angola y los Países Bajos.

facts.statement: Recent discoveries of two nearly complete fossils in Alberta, Canada, including one with fins, provided new data because earlier known fossils only included cranial remains.
facts.quote: El reciente descubrimiento de dos fósiles casi completos (uno de los cuales incluye aletas) en Alberta, Canadá ha dado a los científicos nuevos datos ya que los fósiles conocidos anteriormente solo abarcaban restos craneales.

facts.statement: One fossil specimen contained stomach contents consisting of a marine turtle, large fish, trout, and a possible cephalopod.
facts.quote: Uno de los fósiles tenía además contenidos estomacales, consistentes de elementos pertenecientes a una tortuga marina, peces del tamaño de sábalos y truchas, y un posible cefalópodo.

facts.statement: A fossil found in 2008 and described in 2013 belongs to a 1.8-meter juvenile Prognathodon discovered at the Harrana site in Jordan.
facts.quote: Un hallazgo fósil realizado en 2008 y descrito en 2013, pertenece a un individuo juvenil de Prognathodon de 1,8 metros encontrado en el sitio Harrana en Jordania.

facts.statement: A notable fossil preserved the outline of the tail fin, revealing that Prognathodon had a two-lobed tail resembling an inverted shark tail, which may have helped it emerge and attack prey.
facts.quote: El fósil es notable porque preservó el contorno de la aleta caudal del mosasaurio, revelando que Prognathodon, al igual que Platecarpus y los mosasáuridos tardíos también tenía una aleta caudal con dos lóbulos que se asemejaba a la cola de un tiburón vuelta hacia abajo, cuya forma le puede haber ayudado al animal a emerger así como a atacar a sus presas.

facts.statement: Although Prognathodon was undoubtedly a member of the mosasaurid family, it is not certain which subfamily it belonged to.
facts.quote: Aunque indudablemente Prognathodon era un miembro de la familia de los mosasáuridos, no se sabe con certeza a que subfamilia pertenecía.

facts.statement: Some studies consider Prognathodon a close relative of Mosasaurus, while others classify it as a giant representative of the subfamily Plioplatecarpinae.
facts.quote: Algunos estudios lo han considerado como un pariente cercano de Mosasaurus, mientras que otros lo han considerado como un representante gigante de la subfamilia Plioplatecarpinae.

facts.statement: It has been hypothesized that this genus may have been an ancestor of durophagous mosasauroids like Globidens and Carinodens.
facts.quote: Se ha hipotetizado que este género pudo ser un ancestro de los mosasáuridos durófagos como Globidens y Carinodens.

facts.statement: The type species, Prognathodon solvayi, was described by Louis Dollo in 1889 based on a six-meter specimen found in Belgium with forward-facing front teeth and wrinkled dental enamel.
facts.quote: La especie tipo, Prognathodon solvayi, fue descrita por Louis Dollo en 1889 y se basa en los restos de un ejemplar de unos seis metros de longitud encontrado en Bélgica, con dientes delanteros dirigidos hacia delante y con el esmalte dental fruncido.

facts.statement: The European species P. giganteus had an 85-centimeter skull indicating a length of ten meters, while the larger P. saturator from the Maastrichtian of the Netherlands could reach 14 meters and had very robust jaws with shark bite marks on its skeleton.
facts.quote: Otra especie europea es P. giganteus, dotada de un cráneo de 85 centímetros de largo que indica una longitud de diez metros, y el aun mayor P. saturator, proveniente del Maastrichtiano de los Países Bajos y que podría llegar incluso a los 14 metros de largo, con un esqueleto que tenía rastros de mordidas de tiburones; sus mandíbulas eran muy robustas.

facts.statement: The North American species P. overtoni was 8 meters long, had smooth enamel teeth directed forward unlike other species, and its fossils appear in South Dakota.
facts.quote: P. overtoni, de 8 metros de largo provisto con dientes de esmalte liso y dirigidos hacia adelante a diferencia de las demás especies; sus fósiles aparecen en Dakota del Sur.

facts.statement: The species P. currii found in Israel reached 11 meters in length and had jaws indicating it was a superpredator of marine vertebrates.
facts.quote: P. currii, llegaba a medir 11 metros de largo y estaba dotado de mandíbulas que indican que era un superdepredador de vertebrados marinos.

facts.statement: The New Zealand species P. waiparaensis reached 11 meters in length, had a low skull, and its fossils were found in Maastrichtian strata in the Waipara region of the South Island.
facts.quote: La especie P. waiparaensis de Nueva Zelanda alcanzaba los 11 metros de largo, con un cráneo bajo y sus fósiles se han encontrado en estratos del Maastrichtiano en la región de Waipara en la isla Sur.

facts.statement: The species P. kianda lived during the Maastrichtian, was found in Angola and Namibia, and reached five meters in length.
facts.quote: P. kianda vivió durante el Maastrichtiano y ha sido encontrado en Angola y Namibia, alcanzando los cinco metros de largo.

facts.statement: The species P. sectorius, known mainly from jaws and teeth recovered in New Jersey and the Netherlands, is sometimes attributed to a different genus, Liodon.
facts.quote: P sectorius, conocido principalmente de mandíbulas y dientes recuperados en Nueva Jersey, Estados Unidos y en Holanda, es a veces atribuido a un género distinto, Liodon.

facts.statement: Prognathodon lutugini, more commonly known as Dollosaurus lutugini, was described in 1901 from late Campanian remains from the Donets River in Ukraine.
facts.quote: Prognathodon lutugini - más conocido como Dollosaurus lutugini, fue descrito en 1901 a partir de restos de finales del Campaniano del río Donets en Ucrania.

facts.statement: It was a medium-sized mosasaurid, about 5 meters long, distinguished by the enlargement of the first two pairs of jaw teeth.
facts.quote: Era un mosasáurido de tamaño mediano, de unos 5 metros de largo, que se distinguen por el aumento de los dos primeros pares de dientes de la mandíbula.

facts.statement: There is controversy over whether Prognathodon lutugini belongs to Prognathodon or should be classified as an independent genus.
facts.quote: Existe controversia sobre si pertenece a Prognathodon o se debe clasificar como un género independiente.

facts.statement: The parent group of Prognathodon is Globidensini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Globidensini

facts.statement: Prognathodon belongs to the family Mosasauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Mosasauridae

facts.statement: Prognathodon lived from the Cenomanian to the Danian, between 100.5 and 61.66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Danian (100.5 to 61.66 million years ago)
